root_cause.text: The rt2x00usb driver allocated its `usb_anchor` with `devm_kmalloc()` on the parent `usb_device` (`&usb_dev->dev`) instead of the bound `usb_interface`, so the URB anchor’s lifetime followed the device rather than driver unbind and could leak when the interface was detached without physical disconnect.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `rt2x00dev->anchor = devm_kmalloc(&usb_dev->dev, ...)` to `devm_kmalloc(&usb_intf->dev, ...)`, and the commit message explicitly says USB drivers bind to interfaces and “Fix the USB anchor lifetime so that it is released on driver unbind.”

intent_record.how: This makes the managed allocation tied to the USB interface device rather than the USB device object, so the allocated anchor will be associated with the correct device lifetime and resource-management scope during probe and cleanup.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code already contains the fix for the lifetime/anchor-management issue. In `rt2x00usb_probe()` the anchor is created and initialized with `rt2x00dev->anchor = devm_kmalloc(&usb_dev->dev, sizeof(struct usb_anchor), GFP_KERNEL);` followed by `init_usb_anchor(rt2x00dev->anchor);`, and the URBs are then explicitly anchored/unanchored around submission (`usb_anchor_urb(..., rt2x00dev->anchor);` and `usb_unanchor_urb(...)` on failure). This commit is specifically titled "Use usb anchor to manage URB" and the code no longer shows the old unsafe pattern of leaving URBs unmanaged across disconnect, so the vulnerable construct is not present in this version.
